summary: A foundation model for time series is pretrained once and then asked to forecast series it has never seen, so the evidence for it is its score on held-out datasets. Such datasets are scarce, and a few public leaderboards carry most comparisons, yet none of them states how small a difference its datasets can detect.
takeaways: We call that quantity the resolution of a board and introduce Vernier, a tool that computes it from the files a board already publishes.
GIFT-Eval resolves 6.8 rank places, and its displayed neighbours sit 0.91 apart.
The ten places of its top ten hold fewer than two resolvable steps. fev-bench, Chronos Benchmark II and TIME show the same pattern: their resolution is 3.6 to 19 times the gap between neighbours.
